quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: FDA approves Roche's Enspryng, a first-in-class IL-6R (10-16-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Approval: the U.S. FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an anti-IL-6R monoclonal antibody, for the treatment of adults with thyroid eye disease (TED), following a priority review designation; company: the first and only at-home subcutaneous treatment option for TED, given every four weeks during the maintenance phase and administrable by the patient or a caregiver after training. It is Enspryng's second indication, after neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) approved in 2020. The approval rests on the Phase III SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2 studies: SatraGO-1 did not meet its pre-specified primary efficacy endpoint at Week 24, while SatraGO-2 achieved a significant difference in proptosis response (52.9% vs 23.4% on placebo) and diplopia reduction (60.7% vs 25.8%) in the active TED population, with consistent results in the overall population and no new safety signals. TED affects approximately 155 out of every 100,000 people in the US (company). Enspryng is also under FDA priority review in MOGAD and being studied in additional neurological autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.
quarterly_data.figure: proptosis response 52.9% vs 23.4%; diplopia reduction 60.7% vs 25.8% (SatraGO-2, active TED); second indication; dosing every four weeks (maintenance)
